entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philip of France was a Capetian prince and archdeacon of Paris, born into a powerful dynasty that ruled France from the 10th to the 14th century.

As archdeacon, Philip played a key role in the administration of the Catholic Church in France, and his family's influence extended to the royal court. He was a member of the powerful House of Capet, which produced many notable monarchs, including Hugh Capet and Louis VI.

Philip's significance lies in his connection to the Capetian dynasty and his role in the Church's governance. He is also notable for being a member of the nobility who rose to prominence through his ecclesiastical position.

Philip's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Capetian dynasty on French history and politics, as well as the enduring importance of the Catholic Church in France.

"The order of the Lord is a most excellent thing," Philip of France is quoted as saying, "it is a thing of great honor and of great profit." This statement reflects the importance he placed on his position as archdeacon and his commitment to the Catholic faith.
